subject: Revising partner margin bands and deferred payout cadence
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@anzen.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: align margin bands to retention cohorts (Anzen / Redwood)

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for a productive call yesterday. As discussed, Anzen is seeing strong trial-to-paid conversion for the connectors we co-sell, but churn after month 3 is higher than we modeled. To protect both teams and keep the partnership attractive, our finance team proposed two operational changes:

1) Move part of the commission into a deferred payout that vests at 90 days, tied to net-retention for the customer.
2) Shift the margin bands so higher up-front rates apply for early-stage leads and then step down if retention thresholds aren’t met.

I attached a draft commission schedule (anz-proposed-margin-schedule.xlsx) that shows the proposed bands and a sample waterfall for a $25k ARR deal. We expect this to reduce clawbacks while keeping reps incentivized on acquisition.

Can your partner ops/legal folks review and let us know if Redwood can operationalize deferred payouts at the deal level (HubSpot deal field + payout ledger)? If useful, we can run a short pilot on 10 deals to validate instrumentation.

Appreciate it —
Lara

--
Lara Chen
Head of Partnerships, Anzen Analytics
ops@anzen.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@anzen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: align margin bands to retention cohorts (Anzen / Redwood)

Hi Lara —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the attachment. This direction makes sense from an incentives perspective, and we like the pilot approach. Looping in Marissa (partner ops) to confirm operational feasibility and Karthik for the sales/commission framing.

High-level asks from our side:
- Marissa: can Redwood support a 90-day deferred payment ledger that can be associated to a HubSpot deal id and paid out on a per-deal basis? We need an ops playbook for holdbacks and a reconciliation cadence.
- Legal/Finance: we’ll need a short addendum to the existing reseller/referral agreement to record the deferred payout trigger and clawback terms. I attached a redline template we often start from (redwood-partner-terms-draft-v3.pdf).

If you’re comfortable, we can scope the pilot as: 10 closed-won deals between now and Nov 15, deferred payout window = 90 days, retention metric = net ARR retained at day 90 >= 90% of starting ARR. Payout schedule: 60% on invoice, 40% at day 90 if threshold met.

Next steps: Marissa, can you confirm whether partner billing and partner ledger can track the split and deferred lines? Karthik, any market-level concerns if we publicize these bands to our AE partners?

Best,
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Director, Partner GTM
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@anzen.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: align margin bands to retention cohorts (Anzen / Redwood)

All —

Quick operational readout after reviewing the XLS and chatting with billing: we can implement a deferred payout ledger linked to HubSpot deal ids, but there are three practical considerations:

• Instrumentation: we need a HubSpot property ("partner_payout_status") and a small webhook that updates the ledger when the billing system marks invoice and when a 90-day retention check runs. Ops estimate: 3-4 engineering days + QA.
• Reconciliation cadence: Monthly sweep reconciliations are easiest; we can aggregate held payouts and do a single settlement run for the partner at month-end after the 90-day window completes.
• Accounting/Tax: Deferred payouts create timing differences; finance wants the pilot to stay under $150k gross to avoid changing our revenue recognition process for partner payouts.

Attached is a sample playbook snippet and the adjusted commission matrix with the 60/40 split (anz-proposed-margin-schedule.xlsx). I also added a short template clause for the addendum:

"Deferred payout: Redwood will retain X% of partner commission at close. Retained amounts will be released at day 90 provided the customer retains >=90% net ARR. Any shortfall will be reclaimed by Redwood via crediting future partner payouts or an invoiced clawback at the partner's election."

If Anzen is okay with the pilot guardrails (10 deals, <$150k exposure, 60/40 payout), we can set up the HubSpot fields and a shared Google Sheet for the pilot deals. Legal will prepare an addendum stub to sign.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Partner Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@anzen.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: align margin bands to retention cohorts (Anzen / Redwood)

Thanks — this all looks reasonable. Anzen confirms: pilot accepted under the guardrails (10 deals, <$150k), and we approve the 60/40 (upfront/deferred) structure for pilot deals. Please send the HubSpot property names and the pilot sheet and we’ll populate our 10 candidate deals this week.

Two small asks before we kickoff:
- Can Legal limit the addendum to a 6-month pilot term with an automatic sunset unless both parties agree?
- Can Redwood include a simple opt-out at the partner overlap level so we don’t accidentally apply deferred payouts to deals already under another co-sell arrangement?

If you can get the playbook and HubSpot fields to us by EOD Friday, we’ll start pulling deal candidates.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Lara

--
Lara Chen
Head of Partnerships, Anzen Analytics
lara.chen@anzen.com
